description: Ideal circular membrane (drumhead) modal frequencies. INHARMONIC, like metal, but with its own signature spacing. Multiply each ratio by a chosen fundamental (the (0,1) mode) and place a resonance there. A real drum adds air loading and a kettle, but these ideal ratios are the recognizable skeleton.
source: Standard membrane vibration theory: mode (m,n) frequency = (alpha_mn / alpha_01) * f0, where alpha_mn is the n-th zero of the Bessel function J_m. Rossing & Fletcher, 'The Physics of Musical Instruments', ch. on membranes/timpani.
units: ratio (multiply by fundamental_hz of the (0,1) mode)

q_guidance.note: A free membrane rings moderately; a damped/loaded drumhead is short. Bandwidth sets the ring.

objects.name: ideal circular membrane (uniform tension, no air load)
objects.note: dense, NON-harmonic, no clear pitch — the 'untuned drum' skeleton

objects.name: kettledrum-style (air-loaded; lowest modes pulled toward a near-harmonic 2:3:4:5)
objects.note: air loading shifts the principal (m,1) modes to ~1:1.5:2:2.5:3 -> the timpani's sense of pitch lives here

morph_pairs.name: ideal -> timpani
morph_pairs.motion: dense inharmonic cluster pulls toward the near-harmonic timpani spacing as air loading engages
